facts.statement: Berberosaurus is a genus of theropod dinosaur named after the Berbers of Morocco, found in the Central High Atlas of Morocco.
facts.quote: Berberosaurus (meaning "Berber lizard", in reference to the Berbers of Morocco) is a genus of neotheropod dinosaur, possibly a ceratosaur, from the Toarcian-age (Lower Jurassic) "Toundoute Continental Series" (Azilal Formation) found in the Central High Atlas of Toundoute, Ouarzazate, Morocco.

facts.statement: Berberosaurus is possibly the oldest known ceratosaur, based on partial postcranial remains.
facts.quote: Berberosaurus might be the oldest known ceratosaur, and is based on partial postcranial remains.

facts.statement: Remains of Berberosaurus were discovered during expeditions to the High Atlas starting in the early 2000s over a period of more than six years.
facts.quote: The remains of Berberosaurus were discovered during a series of expeditions to the High Atlas beginning in the early 2000s, where over 6 years, they dug in the local redbeds.

facts.statement: The type specimen is a partial postcranial skeleton of a subadult individual housed in the Muséum d'Histoire Naturelle de Marrakech.
facts.quote: It is based on an associated partial postcranial skeleton of a subadult individual cataloged in the Muséum d'Histoire Naturelle de Marrakech

facts.statement: Berberosaurus fossils were found in bone beds within mudflow deposits alongside Tazoudasaurus and an indeterminate large theropod.
facts.quote: Its remains were found alongside those of Tazoudasaurus and an indeterminate large-bodied theropod within bone beds in mudflow deposits.

facts.statement: New material including an axis, postorbital, cranium, and teeth has been recovered from the same area and is currently under study.
facts.quote: Recent papers have quoted that new material of this genus was recovered on the same area, namely the axis, a postorbital, the cranium and teeth, that are currently being studied.

facts.statement: Berberosaurus is characterized by highly pneumatic cervical vertebrae with short centra and holes in the neural arch, a feature distinct from Elaphrosaurus and Ceratosaurus.
facts.quote: Berberosaurus is characterized by the following features: the cervical vertebra is highly pneumatic, with short cervical centra and holes in the neural arch, with low and short neural spine, unlike Elaphrosaurus and Ceratosaurus.

facts.statement: Distinctive features of Berberosaurus include an arched sacral series, a grooved proximal metacarpal, a femoral trochanter reaching the midpoint of the femoral head, a subtriangular distal tibia, and an oblique ridge covering the fibula's medial sulcus.
facts.quote: It has anteroposteriorly short centra and neural spine; the sacral series markedly arched; the central sacrum narrow transversely; the metacarpal with a very grooved proximal end; anterior femoral trochanter reaches proximally to the midpoint of the femoral head, unlike Ceratosaurus; large femoral trochanteric platform; tibia with subtriangular distal profile; presence of an oblique ridge that covers proximally the medial sulcus of the fibula.

facts.statement: Carrano and Sampson (2008) classified Berberosaurus as a basal ceratosaur outside Neoceratosauria, differing from the abelisauroid classification.
facts.quote: However, Carrano and Sampson (2008) found it to be a basal ceratosaur outside Neoceratosauria instead.

facts.statement: Xu et al. (2009) recovered Berberosaurus as a dilophosaurid in an unresolved polytomy with Dilophosaurus wetherilli, "Dilophosaurus" sinensis, Dracovenator, and Cryolophosaurus.
facts.quote: Subsequently, the analysis of Xu et al. (2009) recovered it as a dilophosaurid in unresolved polytomy with Dilophosaurus wetherilli, "Dilophosaurus" sinensis, Dracovenator and Cryolophosaurus.

facts.statement: Ezcurra, Agnolin, and Novas (2010) placed Berberosaurus in an unresolved polytomy with Ceratosaurus and Abelisauroidea, while the 2018 description of Saltriovenator places it as the sister taxon to Saltriovenator.
facts.quote: The phylogenetic analysis performed by Ezcurra, Agnolin and Novas (2010) recovered Berberosaurus in unresolved polytomy with Ceratosaurus and Abelisauroidea, while the 2018 description of the basal ceratosaur Saltriovenator places Berberosaurus as the sister taxon to that genus.

facts.statement: Berberosaurus liassicus lived during the Early Jurassic, approximately 184 to 176 million years ago, in what is now Africa.
facts.quote: Berberosaurus liassicus ("reptil bereber de liass") es la única especie conocida del género extinto Berberosaurus de dinosaurio terópodo abelisáurido que vivió a principios del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente entre 184 a 176 millones de años, durante el Toarciano, en lo que es hoy África.

facts.statement: Berberosaurus was a moderate-sized bipedal carnivore with a femur 50.5 cm long, estimated to be about 5 meters in total length.
facts.quote: Berberosaurus, como los otros abelisáuridos, fue un carnívoro bípedo Poseía un tamaño moderado; con un fémur de 50,5 centímetros de largo comparables con los largos dados por Gregory S. Paul a animales como Elaphrosaurus de 52,9 cm y Dilophosaurus de 55,0 cm, lo que da una estimación para el largo total de unos 5 metros.

facts.statement: Remains of Berberosaurus were found near those of the early sauropod Tazoudasaurus and another small theropod.
facts.quote: Los restos fueron encontrados cerca de los del saurópodo temprano, el Tazoudasaurus y junto con otro pequeño terópodo, en preparación para su pronta descripción.

facts.statement: Berberosaurus remains were discovered in expeditions to the Toundoute Atlas Mountains near Ouarzazate, Morocco, in the year 2000.
facts.quote: Los restos de Berberosaurus fueron descubiertos en una serie de expediciones a los Montes Atlas Toundoute, cerca de la ciudad de Uarzazat, Marruecos en el 2000.

facts.statement: The remains were found in a bone bed that was once a swamp.
facts.quote: Los restos fueron encontrados en una cama de huesos de lo que fuera un pantano.

facts.statement: Ronan Allain and colleagues described Berberosaurus.
facts.quote: Ronan Allain y colegas describieron a Berberosaurus

facts.statement: It is considered the most basal member of Abelisauroidea, more evolved than Elaphrosaurus, Ceratosauridae, and Spinostropheus, but less evolved than Xenotarsosaurus and Abelisaurus.
facts.quote: como el miembro más basal de Abelisauroidea, más evolucionado que el Elaphrosaurus, los Ceratosauridae, y el Spinostropheus, pero menos que Xenotarsosaurus y Abelisaurus

facts.statement: Berberosaurus differs from other theropods by anatomical details found in the vertebrae, metacarpals, and bones in the hind limbs.
facts.quote: El berberosaurio se diferencia de otros terópodos por detalles anatómicos encontrados en las vértebras, metacarpos, y huesos en los miembros posteriores

facts.statement: Carrano and Sampson in 2008 classified it as a basal ceratosaurid outside Neoceratosauria.
facts.quote: Sin embargo Carrano y Sampson en 2008, lo consideraron como un ceratosáurido basal externo a Neoceratosauria

facts.statement: An analysis by Xu et al. in 2009 recovered it as a dilophosaurid in an unresolved polytomy with Dilophosaurus wetherilli.
facts.quote: Posteriormente, el análisis de Xu et al. de 2009 lo recuperó como un dilofosáurido en politomía no resuelta con Dilophosaurus wetherilli

facts.statement: A phylogenetic analysis by Ezcurra, Agnolin, and Novas in 2010 recovered Berberosaurus in a resolved polytomy with Ceratosaurus and Abelisauroidea.
facts.quote: El análisis filogenético realizado por Ezcurra, Agnolin y Novas en 2010 recuperó a Berberosaurus en una politomía resuelta con Ceratosaurus y Abelisauroidea

facts.statement: The parent group of Berberosaurus is Ceratosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Ceratosauridae

facts.statement: Berberosaurus belongs to the family Ceratosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Ceratosauridae

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Berberosaurus is Berberosaurus liassicus.
facts.quote: Type species: Berberosaurus liassicus

facts.statement: Berberosaurus lived from the Pliensbachian to the Toarcian, between 192.9 and 174.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Pliensbachian to Toarcian (192.9 to 174.7 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Ronan Allain and colleagues classified Berberosaurus as the most basal known abelisauroid, more derived than Elaphrosaurus, Ceratosaurus, and Spinostropheus.
rejected.quote: Ronan Allain and colleagues, who described Berberosaurus, performed a phylogenetic analysis and found their new genus to be the most basal known abelisauroid, more derived than Elaphrosaurus, Ceratosaurus, and Spinostropheus, but less so than Xenotarsosaurus and abelisaurians.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'the most basal known abelisauroid more derived than'

rejected.statement: A 2018 paper found Berberosaurus in different positions, considering it as a basal ceratosaurian, a neoceratosaurian, or a basal abelisauroid.
rejected.quote: Same year, a paper found Berberosaurus in different positions: considered as a basal ceratosaurian, a neoceratosaurian or a basal abelisauroid.
